items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: we had one of the swingingest bands on the South Side... this guy Ellsworth Ellis... we worked, maybe, a week out there

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, that's the date we did. That was about in the winter of '54, I know, when we did that, because, see, I stayed with the man -- in fact, we had one of the swingingest bands on the South Side; we were working; this guy Ellsworth Ellis, Mason has the Flame down in Oakwood, as well as the Basin Street out there on 63rd and Cottage.

And we worked, maybe, a week out there -- then we replaced the band that he had down there at his other club. Dr. Joe Joe Adams had a little show, down at the Flame, and a cat named Benny Kelly -- a comedian -- had a show out there at Basin Street. And our show -- we had Clean Head singing with us, as well as Flynn, featuring the 4 pieces -- they had a thing where Cleanhead they played the opening tune with us on alto, but Griffin did most of the solo.
